transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I guess it’s mostly the tension in my body that finally made me think I should come in. My shoulders and neck are just… clenched all day, like I’m bracing for something, almost like a classroom observation that never actually ends. I try to tell myself it’s not a big deal, but by the evening my jaw aches so much that I can barely enjoy playing guitar. I’m not sure if that’s the sort of thing you mean.
Do you find yourself worrying more days than not about a variety of things, even when there isn’t an immediate stressor?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I try not to make too much of it, and I know everyone worries, but my mind keeps circling through things even when nothing is actually happening right then. Like whether I’ll ever get hired again, or if I’ve somehow ruined my reputation with parents… and then it jumps to retirement slipping away.

Sometimes it even gets kind of embarrassing, like I’ll think maybe one small mistake during a story-time activity means I shouldn’t be trusted with children anymore. I know that probably sounds extreme, but it’s where my mind goes. Does that make sense?
Have you ever experienced sudden episodes where you feel intense fear or discomfort that comes on quickly and peaks within minutes, like a panic attack?

I don’t think so… not in that dramatic, sudden way you’re describing. I mean, I do get worked up and uncomfortable, but I can’t say I’ve noticed it coming out of nowhere and peaking within minutes like that.

Unless I’m misunderstanding what counts as one? I don’t want to answer it wrong.
Do you ever find yourself avoiding certain situations, activities, or even thoughts because they make you feel anxious or uncomfortable?

Yes… I mean, I wouldn’t want to call it “avoidance” too strongly, because I do try to stay involved. But… yes, I guess I have been stepping back from things.

I’ve missed application deadlines because I kept putting off the forms, and interviews haven’t gone very well—I sort of stumble through them once I’m there. And I used to volunteer for story-time more, but now I only really do it if someone else is handling the planning part.

I’m embarrassed to say that, because I do want to get back into the classroom. It’s just… the anxiety gets in the way of doing it reliably. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?
Do you notice that your physical symptoms, like the tension in your neck and jaw, get worse during times of stress or when certain thoughts come up?

Yes… yes, I do. I probably should have said that sooner. It’s not unbearable every minute, but honestly it’s kind of constant.

My shoulders and neck stay clenched most of the day, like I’m bracing for some classroom observation that never actually ends. And when I start thinking about work or whether I’ve made some terrible mistake, it gets worse. By the evening my jaw can ache so much that I don’t even really enjoy playing guitar, which is… frustrating.

I don’t know if that’s the sort of physical thing you mean, but that’s been one of the main reasons I finally thought I should talk to someone.
Have you noticed feeling unusually tired or low on energy lately, even if you haven't been doing anything physically demanding?

I’m not sure I’d say “unusually,” exactly… I mean, I get tired, but I’ve been trying not to make too much of it. I don’t know if it’s more than what anyone would feel when they’re stressed.

There are days I feel sort of worn down even if I haven’t done much physically, but I’m not sure how significant that is. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, even for a few days at a time?

I don’t think so… not in a way I’d want to make too much of. I mean, I have bad days where I feel discouraged or sort of disappointed in myself, but I wouldn’t say hopeless.

And I still care about the things I usually care about. Maybe I don’t always enjoy them as much when I’m preoccupied, but I don’t think I’ve lost interest, exactly. Does that answer it properly?
Do you find yourself feeling keyed up, on edge, or easily startled most days, even when there isn’t an immediate threat or stressor?

I’m not sure… I don’t think I’m easily startled, exactly. Or at least I haven’t noticed that as a big thing.

“Keyed up” is a little harder to answer. I suppose I can feel kind of… alert, maybe too alert, but I don’t know if I’d call it being on edge most days. I might be minimizing it, but I don’t want to overstate it either.

Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?
Do you find yourself feeling restless, like you can’t relax, or like you’re always 'wound up' even when there’s no immediate reason to be?

I guess… yes, maybe more than I’ve wanted to admit. I don’t always think of it as being “wound up,” but my body seems to act like it is.

Honestly, part of what finally made me come in is that my shoulders and neck are clenched almost all day, like I’m bracing for a classroom observation that just never ends. And by the evening my jaw can ache so much that I can barely enjoy playing guitar. I don’t know if that’s exactly what you mean by restless, but it does feel like I can’t fully relax.
Do you find yourself feeling more irritable or easily annoyed, even by small things, when you're feeling anxious or stressed?

I’m not sure I’d call myself irritable, exactly. I mean, I try pretty hard not to let things spill over onto people, especially the kids or coworkers.

But… I suppose when I’m stressed, little things can feel harder to tolerate than they should. I don’t usually snap, at least I hope I don’t, but inside I can get sort of tight and impatient. I’m not sure if that counts as being easily annoyed, though. Does that make sense?
When you're feeling anxious or tense, do you notice any physical reactions like sweating, shaking, or your heart racing, even if it's not during a sudden panic attack?

I don’t think so… not in any clear way, at least. I haven’t really noticed sweating or shaking, and I wouldn’t want to say my heart races if I’m not sure that’s what’s happening.

Sometimes I’m tense enough that I’m aware of my body, but it’s more… just tension, I think. Not like a sudden episode or anything dramatic. Is that still useful to tell you, or are you looking for more obvious reactions?
Do you experience muscle tension or physical symptoms like a clenched jaw or tight shoulders nearly every day, even when there isn’t an immediate stressor?

Yes… I think nearly every day is fair to say. I don’t want to overstate it, but my shoulders and neck are kind of clenched most of the day, even when nothing specific is happening.

It’s like I’m bracing for a classroom observation that never actually comes. And by the evening my jaw can ache enough that it takes some of the enjoyment out of playing guitar. I guess that’s one of the things that made me think maybe I should finally talk to someone about it.
Do you find it difficult to control your worrying, like your anxiety feels constant or uncontrollable, even when you try to focus on something else?

Yes… I think that’s probably true, though I don’t like how it sounds.

I do try to manage it. I’ll tell myself, “Just make a list,” or I’ll pray, or go weed the garden, or try to focus on the next practical thing I can do. And sometimes that helps for a minute. But then one worry sort of hands off to the next one, and before I know it I’ve lost half the afternoon to it.

I’m not trying to just sit around worrying, if that makes sense. It just feels hard to shut off once it gets going.
When you're feeling anxious or tense, do you ever notice symptoms like sweating, heart palpitations, or a feeling of being overly alert, even if it's not during a sudden panic attack?

I’m not sure I can honestly say sweating or palpitations, no. I mean, I might feel tense or keyed up, but I haven’t really noticed my heart pounding or anything like that.

“Overly alert” maybe depends what you mean… I can feel on edge, but I don’t want to label it wrong. If you mean something more obvious or physical, I don’t think I’ve noticed that in a clear way.
